categories.main_business_segments: Cardinal Health operates two primary business segments: Pharmaceutical and Specialty Solutions (Pharma), which distributes branded and generic pharmaceuticals and provides related services in the U.S.; and Global Medical Products and Distribution (GMPD), which manufactures, sources, and distributes Cardinal Health-branded and national brand medical, surgical, and laboratory products globally. Other operating segments include Nuclear and Precision Health Solutions, at-Home Solutions, and OptiFreight Logistics.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced distribution logistics, inventory management systems, and automated technology platforms (such as Wavemark) for inventory management. GMPD manufactures a wide range of medical products, including gloves, surgical drapes, and procedure kits, using both in-house and third-party manufacturing. The Pharma segment utilizes repackaging, specialty pharmaceutical distribution, and data analytics for biopharma solutions.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Cardinal Health serves hospitals, healthcare systems, pharmacies (including retail chains and independents), ambulatory surgery centers, clinical laboratories, physician offices, and patients in the home. Major end markets include acute and non-acute healthcare providers, specialty physician practices, and home healthcare providers. Group purchasing organizations (GPOs) and large retail pharmacy chains are significant customers.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in the United States, with additional operations in Canada, Europe, Asia, Latin America, and other international markets. GMPD has manufacturing facilities in North America, Europe, and Asia, and distributes products globally.
categories.supply_chain_position: Cardinal Health operates primarily as a midstream distributor and logistics provider in the healthcare supply chain, connecting manufacturers with healthcare providers and end users. It also has upstream activities in manufacturing medical products and downstream activities in direct-to-patient home delivery and physician practice management.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding specialty and managed services organizations (MSOs), investing in technology-enabled solutions, and enhancing supply chain efficiency. Recent acquisitions in specialty physician practice management and home healthcare signal a focus on integrated care and specialty growth. R&D is focused on product innovation, digital solutions, and supply chain optimization.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the sale and distribution of pharmaceuticals and medical products, as well as through service fees for logistics, supply chain management, and specialty services. Additional revenue streams include pharmacy management, data analytics, and direct-to-patient medical supply delivery.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Cardinal Health is one of the largest healthcare distributors in the U.S., competing with McKesson Corporation, Cencora (formerly AmerisourceBergen), Medline Industries, and Owens & Minor. It holds a leading position in pharmaceutical distribution and is a major player in medical products manufacturing and distribution, with strong relationships with large retail chains and GPOs.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal 2025, Cardinal Health reported $222.6 billion in revenue, making it one of the largest companies in the healthcare distribution sector. While revenue decreased 2% due to the expiration of a major contract, operating earnings and gross margin increased significantly, driven by specialty and branded pharmaceutical growth and recent acquisitions. The company continues to invest heavily in acquisitions and infrastructure, with a moderate growth trajectory in core areas.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Cardinal Health emphasizes supply chain efficiency, broad product offerings, and integrated solutions that connect manufacturers, providers, and patients. Its scale, technology-enabled logistics, and ability to provide both branded and private-label products, as well as specialty and home healthcare services, differentiate it from competitors. The company highlights cost-effective solutions, reliability, and innovation in care coordination as key value drivers.
